subject: Social Science
central_question: How should development be understood and compared when people have different goals and when income, human well-being and environmental sustainability all matter?
in_scope_units: What Development Promises — Different People, Different Goals: varied and conflicting developmental aspirations
Income and Other Goals: material and non-material dimensions of a good life
National Development: fair and just choices for a country
How to Compare Different Countries or States?: per capita income, averages and distribution
Income and Other Criteria: health, education and comparative state data
Public Facilities: collective provision of essential goods and services
Human Development Report: UNDP, health, education, income and HDI
Sustainability of Development: renewable resources, non-renewable resources, groundwater and crude oil
banned_topics: Detailed classification of primary, secondary and tertiary sectors
Bank credit, collateral and self-help groups

known_pitfalls.claim: Development means the same thing to everyone.
known_pitfalls.correction: People have different and sometimes conflicting developmental goals because their life situations differ.

known_pitfalls.claim: A country with the highest total income is automatically the most developed.
known_pitfalls.correction: Countries are commonly compared using per capita income, and income must also be read with distribution, health and education indicators.

known_pitfalls.claim: A renewable resource can never be depleted.
known_pitfalls.correction: Renewable resources such as groundwater can be overused when extraction exceeds natural replenishment.

recommended_example_progression: Begin with NCERT Table 1.1 on developmental goals of different categories of people.
Use the NCERT Countries A and B average-income example to expose hidden inequality.
Compare Haryana, Kerala and Bihar using NCERT Tables 1.3 and 1.4.
Use NCERT Activity 3 and Table 1.6 to connect nutrition and human development indicators.
Conclude with the NCERT groundwater and crude-oil sustainability examples.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with the section 'EXERCISES', Questions 1–13, followed by an Additional Project / Activity.
